title: Property & Vendor Management for Storage Sites
description: For the people who run a Greens site: the building is the product, and this course teaches how to keep it. Preventive maintenance, every system and what fails, the lot, the trades and their papers, the path from ticket to matched invoice, a vendor on site, inspections and permits, warranty claims, budgets and capital, the Construction Money tab and lien waivers, risk and incidents, and the vendor relationship kept clean.
overview: The four jobs of property management and where the property lives in Nexus
Preventive, corrective and emergency maintenance; Fixed Dates, After Each Completion and By Meter schedules
Every building system, its early signs, the first response and the trade that fixes it
Asphalt, gravel, drainage, canopies, bollards and signs on a vehicle lot
The trades, the four vendor papers, the Compliance tab and the two vendor lists
The one path from ticket to scope, approval, inspection and an invoice matched three ways
A vendor on site: no gate codes, escorted, the visit as a Form
Inspections, permits, the fire cycle and the Records tab
Warranty records and making a claim before paying for a repair
Operating versus capital, the budget by entity, service life and a Construction job
The Construction Money tab: budget, committed, actual, forecast and who sees it
Lien waivers: the four kinds and where they are kept
Vendor performance, contracts, the written trail and the ethics

questions.q: A tenant asks why the gate takes two tries. Which of the four property jobs does a slow gate threaten first?
options: Control the cost
Keep it rentable
Keep the record of every visit the gate vendor made
Protect the asset from a vehicle strike
questions.explanation: A gate that will not work is the product failing in the tenant's hands: keeping it rentable. The record and the cost matter too, but they are not what the tenant feels at the keypad.

questions.q: The Overview of your property shows the gate service as Overdue. Which card are you reading?
options: Critical Items
Open Tickets
Needs Attention
Records Expiring in 90 Days
questions.explanation: The asset Overview card is Needs Attention: overdue preventive tickets and records coming due. Critical Items is the older name; the other two are not cards on the Overview.

questions.q: A $40,000 canopy replacement is clearly needed. Who decides whether it happens this year?
options: You, since the work is at your site and you know the canopy
Leadership, through the capital plan
The canopy vendor who quoted it
Accounting, when the invoice arrives
questions.explanation: Capital work is the owner's decision, made through the budget and the capital plan. The manager builds the case and keeps the old canopy working until then.

questions.q: Door lubrication on rows A to D should happen six months after the last visit, even if the last visit ran late. Which schedule kind fits?
options: Fixed Dates
By Meter
After Each Completion
A calendar reminder in Outlook
questions.explanation: After Each Completion makes the next one due a set time after the last ticket was done. Fixed Dates would keep the original dates even when a visit slipped.

questions.q: The skid steer's service is due every 250 hours. Where does Nexus get the hours?
options: From the asset's own record
From a number typed into the ticket
From the vendor's last invoice
From the operator's time sheet
questions.explanation: A By Meter schedule reads the reading already kept on the asset, so nobody types it twice. The invoice and time sheet are not meter readings.

questions.q: A staff member tries to mark a preventive ticket Resolved with no photo. What happens?
options: It resolves and the record is written
The resolve is refused until a photo is attached
It resolves but the schedule does not move
It resolves; the schedule waits for a photo
questions.explanation: A preventive ticket needs a photo to resolve; the photo is the proof the work was done. Without it, nothing closes and the schedule does not move on.

questions.q: You reset a tripped breaker for the RV row lights and it trips again within the hour. What now?
options: Reset it a third time and watch it
Leave it off and call the electrician
Open the panel to look for scorch marks
Swap it with a breaker from another circuit
questions.explanation: Once is a reset; twice is a fault. Leave it off and call the electrician. Staff never open a panel or swap breakers.

questions.q: After the first heavy rain, water is standing in two ruts on Fairfield's gravel lot. What is the right next step?
options: Wait a week for it to dry out
Fill the ruts with sand from the shop
A ticket for grading where the water stood
Tell tenants in those spaces to park somewhere else for now
questions.explanation: Where water stood after the first rain is where the grading goes next, and standing water a day later is a ticket. Sand in a rut does not restore the crown.

questions.q: A vendor's Compliance tab reads Expired on the morning of a small keypad job. What do you do?
options: Let them work, since the job is small
No work on site until the new paper is filed
Let them work if they promise to email it
Let them work while you call the office
questions.explanation: Expired means no work on site, however small the job, until the new paper is filed. A promise to email it is not a filed paper.

questions.q: You find a landscaper listed under the property's Records > Vendors. Does that mean Greens can pay them?
options: Yes, every vendor on that list is approved
Yes, once you mark the invoice paid there
No, payment needs the Intacct vendor record
Yes, once its contract dates are listed
questions.explanation: Records > Vendors is the property's own list of who services it. The vendor Greens pays is the Intacct vendor record in Accounting > Records > Vendors, with its papers.

questions.q: A new roofer is good, licensed and cheap, but has no certificate naming Greens as additional insured. What does that certificate do for Greens?
options: Lets Greens claim on the roofer's policy directly
Proves the roofer's license is current
Covers the roofer's crew if one is hurt
Proves the roofer's crew is covered if one of them is hurt
questions.explanation: Additional insured status lets Greens claim on the vendor's policy directly. The license, workers comp and W-9 are the other three papers, each with its own job.

questions.q: A tenant's unit has water on the floor after rain, and the vendor finds the gutter above it clogged. Which part of the job is the inspection?
options: Reading the vendor's invoice
Checking the work against the scope and photographing it
Approving the vendor's quote on the ticket before the visit is booked
Calling the tenant to say it is fixed
questions.explanation: The inspection is checking the finished work against the scope, testing it and photographing it. Approval comes before the work; the invoice comes after.

questions.q: An invoice arrives reading only "gate repair, Temecula." What makes it matchable in one look?
options: The vendor's tax ID on the invoice
The ticket number on the invoice
A photo of the gate stapled to it
The site manager's signature on it
questions.explanation: The ticket number ties the invoice to the approved scope and quote (what was ordered) and the inspection photo (what was received). Ask every vendor to put it on the invoice.

questions.q: The gate vendor at 7:55 AM asks for the code "so I don't have to bother you." What is right?
options: Give it, since this vendor is trusted
Staff open the gate; no code given
Give it, then change the code tomorrow
Give it, then change the code after the vendor has left
questions.explanation: A vendor never gets a gate code. Staff open the gate. A standing code lets a vendor come at 2:00 AM.

questions.q: The fire inspector arrives and an alarm panel is beeping. What do you do?
options: Silence it before the walk starts
Tell the inspector and call the vendor
Close the sprinkler valve to stop it
Silence it and call the vendor later
questions.explanation: Never silence a panel or close a valve to make an inspection look better. A false record is worse than a failed inspection.

questions.q: A gate operator installed last spring fails. A different gate vendor quotes $1,100 to fix it today. What comes first?
options: Approve the quote; the gate is down
Check Records > Warranties for the operator
Ask Accounting whether there is budget
Get two more quotes before you decide
questions.explanation: Check for a warranty before approving any repair. If it is covered, the claim goes to the party named on it, and another vendor's work could void it.

questions.q: A new gate operator replaces one that failed after many years. How is that money classed?
options: Operating expense, the month it is paid
Capital, depreciated over its life
A repair, since a gate already existed
A reserve, since money was set aside
questions.explanation: Replacing something that lasts years is capital, recorded as an asset and depreciated. The reserve is the money saved for it, not the expense itself.

questions.q: Where are a property's actual maintenance costs read from for its budget?
options: The property's Project-Job code
Its Intacct entity, by vendor and account
The property's Project-Job code in Intacct
The ticket totals in Nexus
questions.explanation: A property is an entity in Intacct, so its costs are read by entity. Project-Job codes belong to Construction jobs, not properties.

questions.q: A crew lead on a Construction job asks why he cannot see the Money tab. What is the answer?
options: A fault to report to IT
Money shows only to the job's managers
The job is not mapped to Intacct yet
It shows only after IT grants access
questions.explanation: Money is shown to the job's own managers and Manager-tier people in the job's company. Crews never see it; that is the rule working.

questions.q: Actual to Date on a job includes a camera invoice that belongs to another property. What do you do?
options: Type a corrected Actual to Date
Click the figure, read the line, ask Accounting
Delete the commitment it came from
Edit the line in the Money tab
questions.explanation: Money is never typed into Nexus. Posted figures open their ledger lines; a line that does not belong is Accounting's to recode.

questions.q: A sub's invoice arrives with a Conditional Progress waiver. When do you expect the Unconditional Progress?
options: Along with the next invoice's quote
After this payment has cleared
Only at the end of the whole job
Never; a conditional waiver is enough for the payment
questions.explanation: Conditional with the invoice, unconditional once paid. The unconditional waiver is what protects the property.

questions.q: A sub asks you to type up a waiver for them to sign. What is right?
options: Write one from a template online
Ask for their own signed form instead
Copy last month's waiver and change the date
Skip the waiver this time
questions.explanation: Nexus never writes waiver wording; several states require statutory forms word for word. The vendor supplies its own signed form, and you attach it.

lessons.title: Words to Know
lessons.summary: The property, vendor, money and insurance words of this course, in the Academy Glossary.

questions.q: You are new at a site. A tenant complains about a door, the lot floods in one corner, and a light is out. What does the site sell that all three threaten?
options: Units at the best rate in town
Space that is dry, secure and reachable
Insurance and locks at the counter
Fast, friendly service at the front desk every day
questions.explanation: A storage site sells dry, secure, reachable space; the building is the product, so each failure is the product failing.

questions.q: A vendor offers to start a $3,000 roof repair today if you sign. Nothing like it is in the budget. What is right?
options: Sign; it is your site
Ask the manager above you first
Sign and tell them next week
Have the vendor ask Accounting to approve it for you
questions.explanation: When in doubt, ask up. Spending beyond your limit and outside the plan is the owner's decision; signing for it is not the manager's job.

questions.q: A problem a staff member texts you about counts as recorded, as long as you keep the text.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Every problem is a ticket. A ticket has a number, an owner, a due date and a history; a text has none, and the next manager cannot read it.

questions.q: The same door latch has failed three times this year. What is the best response?
options: Fix it again and keep an eye on it
Make it a preventive schedule, with the reason
Replace every latch on the row
Tell the tenant to use a different door
questions.explanation: Two of the same ticket is the signal. A schedule with the reason written in it survives the next manager.

questions.q: Extinguisher service is due every November by law, and last year's visit ran three weeks late. Which kind keeps it on the November date?
options: After Each Completion
Fixed Dates
By Meter
No schedule; a ticket each year
questions.explanation: Fixed Dates is due on set dates whether or not the last one is done. After Each Completion would let a late visit push next year's due date.

questions.q: You notice a due preventive ticket seems missing and start filing one by hand. What should you check first?
options: Whether the vendor is free to come out that same week
Whether the schedule already filed one
Whether the budget allows it
Whether the photo is ready
questions.explanation: A due date is never filed twice. Look for the ticket the schedule already filed before raising a second one by hand.

questions.q: The gate failed at 9:00 PM on a Saturday after weeks of grinding. What kind of maintenance was the grind asking for?
options: Emergency
Preventive or corrective
Capital replacement
None; older gates grind, it is normal
questions.explanation: Every emergency was once a corrective job, and every corrective job was once preventive work nobody did. The grind was the warning.

questions.q: A roll-up door drifts down on its own and the tenant asks you to tighten the spring. What do you do?
options: Tighten it with the right tool
Report it; the spring is the door vendor's
Tighten it carefully if you have the right tool for it
Ask the tenant to hold it
questions.explanation: A spring under tension can break a wrist or worse. It is the door vendor's alone; report it and mark the unit if it cannot be secured.

questions.q: A tenant says heat damaged a piano in the climate building in August. What answers the claim?
options: The thermostat's setting
The building's temperature log
The HVAC vendor's opinion
The tenant's own photos from move-in
questions.explanation: A daily reading at the same spot and hour is the proof the building stayed in range. A setting says what was asked for, not what happened.

questions.q: The gate will not close at night. Your manager agrees it goes on manual. What else must you know about the gate?
options: Where the manual release is
How to adjust the drive chain
How to open the operator housing
How to rewire the gate keypad
questions.explanation: Know the manual release and the sign that goes up when it is used. Adjusting a chain under tension or opening the housing is never staff work.

questions.q: You need to see whether gutters on a two-story building are full. What is right?
options: A ladder and a phone camera
Ask the roofing vendor to photograph it
Climb the roof from the inside stairs
Use a ladder, a harness from the shop and a phone camera
questions.explanation: Nobody goes on a roof without fall protection and training. Ask the vendor for photos.

questions.q: A bollard at the end of a canopy row is bent from a rig. What is right?
options: Straighten it and repaint it
Replace it
Leave it, it still stands
Add a second one beside it
questions.explanation: A bent bollard did its job and has lost its strength; it is replaced, never straightened.

questions.q: A tenant's 12x45 space in Cubby is painted 12x40 on the lot. What caused this, and how is it prevented?
options: Normal; paint wears down over time
Striping not taken from the space map
Cubby rounds sizes on move-in
The tenant measured from the wrong line
questions.explanation: Stripe from the system's space map and check it with a measuring wheel afterward. A mismatch is a dispute on move-in day.

questions.q: A canopy repair changed the beam height on row C. What must happen before a tall rig parks there?
options: Nothing, the old sign stands
Re-measure and update both clear height signs
Tell each tenant the new height
Post the new height in Cubby only
questions.explanation: Every row carries its measured clear height on both ends; re-measure after any canopy work.

questions.q: Crack seal can wait a few years as long as the asphalt looks fine from the office.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Water gets under the surface through cracks long before the lot looks bad. Skipping crack seal makes the next, costlier step come sooner.

questions.q: Accounting says a new vendor cannot be paid yet. Which missing paper most likely explains it?
options: The W-9
The license
Two references
The written scope
questions.explanation: No W-9, no payment: Accounting cannot pay a vendor it cannot report. The other papers matter for working on site.

questions.q: A vendor's papers show Expiring Soon. Can they work today, and what do you do?
options: No; send them home until renewed
Yes; ask for the renewal now
Yes; nothing to do until it expires
No; they need a new license first
questions.explanation: Expiring Soon may still work. Ask for the renewal now so it is not Expired on the morning of the next visit.

questions.q: The same vendor papers show on a Construction job's Subs tab and on the vendor's Compliance tab in Accounting.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: There is one set of papers per vendor, read in both places. Nobody keeps a second copy.

questions.q: A vendor's address changed. You edit it on the vendor's record in Accounting. What does the record show next?
options: The new address, live at once
Pending Approval
Declined
Changed In Intacct
questions.explanation: An edit becomes a request: Pending Approval, then Approved - Awaiting Intacct until it is keyed in, then In Intacct. Intacct stays the source of truth.

questions.q: A canopy repair quotes at $9,000. The site's limit is $5,000. Splitting it into two $4,500 tickets would be what?
options: Two small jobs
One job, splitting a control
A normal practice
Fine, as long as both tickets are approved
questions.explanation: A job split into two tickets to stay under a limit is still one job, and splitting it breaks the approval control.

questions.q: When does a vendor job count as done?
options: When the vendor leaves the property and says it is finished
When you have checked it against the scope and photographed it
When the invoice arrives
When the tenant stops calling
questions.explanation: Walk the work with the scope in hand, test it, photograph it, then Mark Resolved. If it does not meet the scope, the ticket stays open.

questions.q: An invoice matches the quote and the ticket number, but the ticket has no finished-work photo. Which of the three matches is missing?
options: What was ordered
What was received
What was billed
None; it can be paid
questions.explanation: What was received is the inspection and finished-work photo on the ticket. Without it, the invoice waits.

questions.q: The gate is stuck open at 10:00 PM and the approved vendor answers. What can you skip tonight?
options: The ticket
The quotes
Telling your manager
The photos
questions.explanation: An emergency skips the quotes, never the record. Raise the ticket, take the photos, tell your manager the same day; the invoice is reviewed after.

questions.q: A job has left the building and you are waiting for the vendor's visit Thursday. How do you show that in the ticket?
options: Leave it Open; note the date in your calendar
Set Waiting for Vendor with the vendor and date
Mark Resolved and reopen Thursday
Set On Hold until Thursday
questions.explanation: Waiting for Vendor, with the vendor's name and promised date written in, lets the desk and your manager see where it stands without a call.

questions.q: A site manager may pay a small vendor invoice with the site's petty cash if the work was inspected.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The site never pays a vendor, whatever the size. Accounting pays against a matched invoice.

questions.q: A vendor needs a rented unit opened to reach a leak behind its wall. The tenant cannot be reached. What is right?
options: Open it with the vendor, since the leak is spreading to the next unit
Only with an emergency the manager approved, a witness and photos
Cut the lock and tell the tenant later
Have the vendor reach through the next unit
questions.explanation: A rented unit is opened only with the tenant's written consent, or an emergency the manager approved, with a witness and photos. The tenant has exclusive control.

questions.q: The paving vendor needs a space cleared, and a tenant's trailer is in it. Who moves the trailer?
options: Staff, with the tenant's spare key
The tenant
The vendor, carefully
A tow company
questions.explanation: Tenants' vehicles are never moved by vendors or staff. The tenant moves it.

questions.q: Where do you tick the vendor-visit checklist?
options: In a text message to your manager
In a Form from Fill a Form
On a paper sheet kept at the front desk
In the ticket's own checklist
questions.explanation: The visit's checklist is a Form, filled on the phone, with photos, working offline. The ticket stays the record of the job.

questions.q: When do you check a vendor's Compliance tab for a booked visit?
options: When the visit is booked
The morning of the visit
Once a year
Only if the vendor is new
questions.explanation: Papers lapse between booking and the visit. Check that morning; Expired does not unload.

questions.q: Which of these usually needs a permit?
options: Replacing a faded panel in an existing sign
A new light pole and circuit
A like-for-like roof panel
Crack seal and striping
questions.explanation: New circuits, panels and light poles usually need a permit. Like-for-like repairs and asphalt maintenance usually do not.

questions.q: A buyer's lender asks about an electrical permit pulled two years ago that never had its last inspection. What is the problem?
options: Nothing; the work was already done
An open permit, never finaled
Nothing; permits close by themselves after a year
The vendor kept the permit papers
questions.explanation: A permit that never passed its last inspection is open, and that is a problem at sale, at refinance and at a claim.

questions.q: The fire inspector's notice lists three items with deadlines. When do you raise the tickets?
options: The week before each deadline
That afternoon, one per item
After the reinspection, once you know what still fails
When the vendor is free to come
questions.explanation: Raise a ticket for each item with its deadline the same day, close each with a photo, and file the closed notice in Records.

questions.q: A record in Records with a next date shows on the property's Needs Attention card well before it is due.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Dated records warn about 90 days ahead, so nothing lapses because nobody remembered.

questions.q: A warranty in Records shows Incomplete. What does that mean?
options: The warranty was refused
Its scope or expiration is missing
The vendor went out of business
It expires within 90 days and needs renewing
questions.explanation: Incomplete means the scope or the expiration is missing, so it cannot be tracked. Fill the missing field from the paper.

questions.q: A skid steer has a manufacturer's warranty. Where should it be recorded?
options: A new Warranties list in a spreadsheet
On the skid steer's record in Item Management
In a new Warranties list for equipment on the property
In the vendor's Compliance tab
questions.explanation: Equipment warranties live on the equipment's Item record. Never a second list.

questions.q: A warranty claim for a failed roof seam is refused because the roof was never serviced. What could have saved it?
options: A quicker phone call
The preventive tickets with their photos
A second roofer's opinion
A higher priority and a faster response on the ticket
questions.explanation: Many warranties require proof of maintenance; the closed preventive tickets and their photos are that proof.

questions.q: Letting a different vendor repair a part under warranty can void the warranty.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Claim through the party named on the warranty. Another vendor's work on a covered part can void it.

questions.q: Leadership asks why the gate line is over budget by March. What is the best move?
options: Wait for year end, when the whole picture is in the books
Explain the variance now, from the tickets
Move the cost to another line
Ask the vendor to bill later
questions.explanation: A line over by March is a conversation in March. Explain it from the record.

questions.q: The emergency spend line keeps rising. What does it most likely mean?
options: Vendors raised their prices
The preventive schedules are wrong or skipped
The budget was too generous
Tenants are wearing the site out faster
questions.explanation: Every emergency dollar is a preventive dollar nobody spent.

questions.q: A manager has patched the Building C roof five times in two years. What should come next?
options: A sixth patch, it is cheaper
A capital case with the tickets and age
A new roofing vendor
Keep patching until it fails
questions.explanation: Patching a capital problem with operating money delays a decision that is coming anyway. Build the case for the capital plan.

questions.q: A job's Pending Changes show $6,800 for a revised footing. Why does it matter before the work is done?
options: It is already in Actual to Date
It pushes the forecast up until decided
It is paid from the site's budget
It replaces a commitment automatically
questions.explanation: Forecast at Completion takes Budget plus Pending Changes when that is larger, so an undecided change is tomorrow's overrun.

questions.q: A commitment with a vendor on the job ends early. What happens to its row?
options: It is deleted
It is set to Void and stays on the record
It is moved to the Trash
It is deleted, with a note in the job's activity log
questions.explanation: Nothing is deleted. A commitment that ends is Void, and the record keeps it.

questions.q: Where does Billed to Date on a commitment come from?
options: Typed in from the vendor's invoice
Read from the books for that vendor and job
The site manager's estimate
The commitment less retainage held
questions.explanation: Billed to Date is read from Intacct, never typed, and opens the lines behind it.

questions.q: Why does a property owner collect lien waivers from a sub at all?
options: They are required to start work
An unpaid sub or supplier can lien the property
They replace the certificate of insurance
They prove the sub carries insurance
questions.explanation: An unpaid contractor or supplier can place a mechanics lien on the property itself. Waivers prove each payment cleared that right.

questions.q: The steel sub sends its last invoice. Which waiver should come with it?
options: Unconditional Progress
Conditional Final
Unconditional Final
Conditional Progress
questions.explanation: Conditional with the invoice, unconditional once paid. With the last invoice, that is the Conditional Final.

questions.q: A waiver arrives with the amount left blank. What do you do?
options: Fill in the invoice amount yourself
Send it back to the vendor
Attach it; the invoice shows the amount
Accept it as long as it is signed
questions.explanation: Never edit or complete a vendor's waiver. Anything wrong or blank goes back to the vendor before Accounting pays.

questions.q: A Construction job can be closed out while one commitment still lacks its Unconditional Final waiver.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A job is not closed out until every commitment has its Unconditional Final on file.

questions.q: A storm drops a roof panel on a tenant's trailer. Whose insurance answers for the trailer?
options: Greens' property policy
The tenant's own protection or policy
The roofer who installed the panel, through their policy
Greens' liability policy
questions.explanation: Loss of a tenant's goods goes to the tenant's own protection plan or policy; the lease limits Greens' liability. Never promise the property will cover it.

questions.q: The roofer can replace storm-damaged panels today. The carrier has not seen them. What is right?
options: Replace them now to stop the rain
Tarp only; wait for the manager's go-ahead
Replace them before more rain gets in
Replace them and photograph the new ones
questions.explanation: Temporary protection only. Permanent repairs wait until the manager above you says so; the adjuster may need to see the damage.

questions.q: A vendor's truck cracks a block wall and the crew lead offers to just fix it. What do you do?
options: Accept; it saves a claim
Photograph, ticket, tell your manager
Accept, if it is done this week
Accept, as long as the work is done this week
questions.explanation: A quiet fix leaves no claim and no record. The damage goes to the vendor's insurer through the certificate.

questions.q: After an incident on the lot, when do you ask for the camera footage to be saved?
options: The same hour
At the end of the week
When the insurer asks
Only if someone was hurt
questions.explanation: Recorders overwrite. Tell your manager which camera and what time, the same hour.

questions.q: A tenant who just backed into a canopy post asks, "Will your insurance handle this?" What do you say?
options: "Yes, we're covered for this."
"I'm documenting it for my manager."
"It was the post's fault, really."
"Don't worry, the property will take care of it."
questions.explanation: Never promise payment, admit or assign fault, or keep it off the record. Say what you saw and pass it up.

questions.q: A gift box from a vendor arrives at your home. What is right?
options: Keep it; it is the holidays
Return it, note it, tell your manager
Share it with the site staff
Keep it and send a thank-you note
questions.explanation: No gifts beyond a cup of coffee. Say no, write it on the vendor's record and tell the manager above you.

questions.q: Which system most needs a service contract rather than on-call work?
options: Signage
The gate
Locksmith
Waste pickup
questions.explanation: A contract fits a system with both schedules and emergencies, like the gate. On-call fits trades needed a few times a year.

questions.q: You want to drop the gate vendor after two late emergencies. What must be true first?
options: The contract has expired
A second gate vendor is qualified
Accounting has deleted the record
The vendor's contract has run out at the end of the year
questions.explanation: Never leave a gap in gate coverage. Feedback first, a second vendor qualified, and the old record kept.

questions.q: You agreed a visit date with a vendor by phone. Where does that agreement go?
options: Nowhere; a call is enough
A line in the ticket
The notes app on your phone
A text message to the vendor
questions.explanation: The trail is the ticket and the email or Teams thread. A call is followed by a line in the ticket.

questions.q: Your brother-in-law's paving company quotes lowest for the sealcoat. What must you do?
options: Hire them; the price is lowest
Disclose it in writing to your manager
Hire them under a different name
Hire them, since price is what counts
questions.explanation: Undisclosed interest is a conflict whatever the price. Tell the manager above you in writing.

questions.q: A vendor is at the gate and you need their papers fast. Where do you look?
options: Records > Vendors on the property
Accounting > Records > Vendors > Compliance
The property's Records > Vendors list, under the vendor's name
Item Management
questions.explanation: The papers that decide whether a vendor may work are on the Intacct vendor's Compliance tab.

questions.q: Put the first three steps of a paid repair in order.
options: Ticket, then warranty check, then scope
Scope, then ticket, then quote
Quote, then ticket, then scope
Approval, then a ticket, then a scope, then the warranty
questions.explanation: Ticket first, then check for a warranty before any paid repair, then the scope that quotes and inspection run against.

questions.q: On a job's Money tab, a change order that was approved is already inside the Budget figure.
